title: Chinese Pidgin English - Wikipedia
text: Chinese Pidgin English is a pidgin language lexically based on English, but influenced by a Chinese substratum. From the 17th to the 19th centuries, there was also Chinese Pidgin English spoken in Cantonese-speaking portions of China.

title: APiCS Online - Survey chapter: Chinese Pidgin English
text: Chinese Pidgin English is one of the earliest pidgin languages to be documented. The term “pidgin” itself is first attested in Chinese Pidgin English, and the influence of the language extends to contact languages such as Hawai'i Creole and Melanesian Pidgin (Tok Pisin, Bislama).

title: What Is a Pidgin Language?
text: Hawaiian Pidgin is actually a creole language (Hawaiian Creole English), but is still commonly called “Pidgin” by its speakers. In Papua New Guinea, Tok Pisin is a creole, yet it’s often simply referred to as “Pidgin.”
